title: V and W
what: swapping or merging /v/ and /w/ ('wery well', 'vine' for 'wine')
summary: The subtle distinction between /v/ and /w/ often remains challenging for advanced learners due to native language interference. This persistent error can obscure meaning and detract from the speaker's professional credibility.
listenFor: Pay close attention to whether your upper teeth touch your lower lip for /v/, or if your lips round without touching for /w/.

contrasts.wrong: We went to a wery interesting wiewpoint.
contrasts.right: We went to a very interesting viewpoint.
contrasts.note: /v/ requires upper teeth on lower lip; /w/ uses rounded lips.

contrasts.wrong: He wore a wery warm west.
contrasts.right: He wore a very warm vest.
contrasts.note: The sounds are distinct and not interchangeable.

contrasts.wrong: We need to wote on the new wision.
contrasts.right: We need to vote on the new vision.
contrasts.note: Clear articulation of /v/ and /w/ is crucial for clarity.

contrasts.wrong: She was wery well-wersed in the subject.
contrasts.right: She was very well-versed in the subject.
contrasts.note: Practice the distinct mouth positions for /v/ and /w/.
